column1: # verify-fuzz-corpus.tsv — standing adversarial corpus for the verify pre-exec gate.
# Language-neutral fixture (plain TSV, no quoting rules): the Go port reuses
# this file unchanged. One case per line, fields separated by a single TAB:
#   id      stable case id (F-R* refuse, F-X* expected-fail, F-P* pass).
#   expect  what the gate must do: one of verify-destructive,
#           (refuse with exactly this typed code), or PASS (execute).
#           For xfail rows expect is aspirational: the code the gate SHOULD
#           refuse with once the gap is closed.
#   mode    strict (violation fails the suite) or xfail (known gap: executing
#           is the recorded expectation; refusing is an XPASS that fails the
#           suite with a "promote to strict" message).
#   command single-line verifyCmd. No tabs, no newlines. Targets are
#           so executed rows stay hermetic and fast.
# How to extend: append one line. New hostile shape that the gate already
# refuses -> strict with the typed code. New hostile shape that EXECUTES
# (a bypass) -> xfail with the aspirational code, never a gate fix in the
# corpus ticket; the gate fix (if any) lands separately and promotes the
# row to strict. Benign command the gate must not catch -> PASS.
# Coverage: quoting/case/prefix mutations, pipe-wrapper smuggling, loader
# and config smuggling, remote-execution flags, exfiltration shapes, plus
# benign commands pinning the false-positive boundary. The V1-V40
# regression legs stay pinned in evals/cases/verify-allowlist.sh; this file
# is the mutation battery on top of them.
